promise: A visitor can browse the full service catalog as a grid of cards showing title, thumbnail, vendor, price and rating.
ux_bar: Grid renders 2/3/4 columns per wpss_archive_service_columns and collapses to one column under 640px with no horizontal scroll. A service with no featured image shows a placeholder, never a broken image.

promise: A visitor can filter the catalog by category, including subcategories grouped under their parent.
ux_bar: Subcategories are selectable (grouped under their parent via wpss_group_category_terms), and choosing one PRESERVES any active sort and keyword search rather than resetting them.
notes: Full page GET-form reload, not AJAX - there is no spinner state between submit and reload.

promise: A visitor can narrow the catalog by minimum and maximum price.
ux_bar: Applying a price filter keeps the active category, sort and keyword (carried as hidden fields) instead of silently dropping them.

promise: A visitor can filter by minimum star rating and by delivery-time band.
ux_bar: A filter combination with zero matches shows the catalog empty state WITH a clear-filters path, never a blank page the visitor has to back out of.

promise: A visitor can sort the catalog by newest, rating, or price low-to-high / high-to-low.
ux_bar: After reload the dropdown shows the applied sort as selected - the control never reads 'default' while the results are sorted otherwise.

promise: A visitor can search the catalog by keyword.
ux_bar: A zero-result search shows the designed empty state (icon, explanation, a way to clear the search), not a bare empty grid.

promise: A visitor can run one search that returns both matching services AND matching vendors.
ux_bar: DEAD ON WEB. A buyer typing a vendor's name into the catalog search box gets zero results even though a matching vendor exists, and nothing signals that a vendor search exists at all. Either wire this endpoint to the search box or state that catalog search is services-only.
notes: MISSING frontend wiring. Verified 2026-09-19: route registered at src/API/API.php:387; grep of templates/ and assets/js/ finds zero callers. API/mobile-only today.

promise: A visitor can open a service and see gallery, description, packages, FAQs, reviews and the vendor card.
ux_bar: Every hooked section degrades gracefully when empty - no FAQs configured hides the whole FAQ block rather than rendering an empty accordion header.

promise: A visitor can browse the service gallery, and a showcase video does not contact YouTube until they ask for it.

entry_points.admin: Service editor gallery metabox / wizard Gallery step

ux_bar: The gallery opens on an image, the video's poster leads the strip, and the embed lives in a <template> so no third-party request fires until play is clicked. A duplicate attachment must not produce an empty tile.
notes: Frontend dedupes gallery ids via array_unique - the 1.7.2 duplicate-image defect was in the WIZARD, not here (see WIZ-03).

promise: A buyer can compare tiered packages and select one before ordering.
ux_bar: Switching a package tab updates price, delivery days and revision count TOGETHER in one action - never a stale price beside a new tier's delivery time.

promise: A buyer can add optional paid add-ons before checkout.
ux_bar: Add-ons chosen in the modal appear on the checkout summary line by line with individual prices, never folded silently into the package total.
notes: Historic meta-key mismatch between wizard-authored and admin-authored add-ons; unified via wpss_get_service_extras().

promise: A visitor can expand and collapse each FAQ.
ux_bar: aria-expanded toggles per question so a screen reader announces open/closed, and only the clicked FAQ opens.

promise: A visitor can read reviews and load more without a full page reload.
ux_bar: Load more disables with a loading label while in flight, then appends or HIDES ITSELF once a partial page returns - it never keeps offering more past the last review.

promise: A logged-in visitor can mark a review helpful.
ux_bar: The count updates in place on click, and a second click is refused SERVER-side with a clear 'already marked' rather than only visually disabled or silently double-counting.
notes: Increment is an atomic UPDATE, not read-then-write - safe under concurrent clicks.

promise: A logged-in visitor can favorite or unfavorite a service from the archive card, the service page, or the dashboard, with consistent state everywhere.

entry_points.frontend: card heart, single service heart, dashboard/favorites remove

ux_bar: Filled/outline state and aria-pressed flip on click and MATCH the server on next load - a heart that looks favorited but did not persist never occurs, because state comes back in the same response.
notes: One canonical implementation since 1.2.0; a duplicate dead handler in single-service.js was removed.

promise: A buyer can see all saved services in one paginated dashboard list and remove any of them.
ux_bar: 20 per page with prev/next - 100+ favorites never trigger an unpaginated query. Removing the last item on a page shows the updated empty state, not a stuck loader.

promise: A visitor sees the seller's identity, rating, join date and a portfolio sample on the service page.

entry_points.frontend: sidebar vendor card / About the Seller

ux_bar: Vendor stats come from the one canonical profile source everywhere they appear (schema markup, REST, card, checkout sidebar) - a buyer never sees two different 'member since' dates for the same vendor.
notes: Previously fragmented across dead legacy user-meta; single-sourced via wpss_get_vendor().

promise: A buyer can add a service with its chosen package and add-ons to the cart.

entry_points.api: POST wpss/v1/cart/add REGISTERED BUT UNUSED by web; web uses admin-ajax wpss_add_service_to_cart

ux_bar: A logged-out visitor is never dead-ended - the server returns a checkout URL carrying the selection so the account step happens at checkout, not at wp-login.php.
notes: REST/AJAX duplication. Not customer-facing today, but two implementations of one flow violate the plugin's own one-flow rule and can drift.

promise: A buyer can view cart contents with thumbnails, titles and per-item price before checking out.

entry_points.api: GET wpss/v1/cart exists but this template does not use it

ux_bar: At 540px the image shrinks and the remove control moves to its own row rather than overflowing horizontally.

promise: A buyer can remove a cart item without leaving the page.

entry_points.api: DELETE wpss/v1/cart/{item_key} REGISTERED BUT UNUSED by web

ux_bar: The row animates out and the header cart badge updates in the same response; removing the last item reloads to the empty-cart state rather than leaving a blank column beside a populated total.
notes: Same REST/AJAX duplication as CART-01.

promise: A buyer with an empty cart sees a helpful empty state that routes them back to browsing, not an error.

entry_points.frontend: /cart/ with 0 items, and checkout reached empty

ux_bar: Cart and checkout use the IDENTICAL empty-state shape (icon, title, explanation, Browse Services CTA) - reaching checkout with nothing selected must not read as a buyer-caused error.

promise: A buyer with several cart items is told at checkout that only the current service is being paid for and the rest remain.
ux_bar: The notice names the remaining count and the current service by name, so a buyer never wonders whether the other items were dropped or will be double-charged.

promise: A buyer can review service, billing, payment method and total on one checkout screen and pay.

roles.anon: can when guest checkout is on

ux_bar: The Pay button total, the summary total and the amount actually charged are ONE figure computed once by wpss_calculate_tax - never three numbers that can drift.

promise: A logged-out buyer can complete checkout without a separate registration step; an account is created from the billing details they already typed.
ux_bar: A notice ABOVE the billing fields says an account will be created and a password email will follow - before they submit, never as a post-payment surprise. The order's customer_id is a real user from the first moment, never 0.

promise: With guest checkout disabled, a logged-out buyer sees a sign-in wall rather than a broken payment form.
ux_bar: Logging in from the wall returns to the SAME checkout URL with the package and add-on selection intact, not to a generic dashboard.

promise: Name and email are always collected; the owner configures which additional billing fields are required.
ux_bar: A returning customer with a saved profile sees the billing block collapsed to a summary rather than retyping the same fields every purchase.

promise: A buyer sees tax itemised as its own line before paying, at the rate the settings define.
ux_bar: The tax line appears ONLY when tax_amount > 0 - a 0% config never shows a '$0.00 Tax' row. The displayed rate and label match exactly what wpss_calculate_tax() charges; the display figure is never computed separately.
notes: No coupon/discount capability exists anywhere in Free - confirmed by grep. Out of scope, not a gap.

promise: A buyer can choose among the payment methods the owner enabled: Stripe, PayPal or Offline.
ux_bar: Selecting a method reveals only that gateway's fields beneath it (accordion, not all forms stacked), and only one gateway's JS owns the submit button (data-wpss-own-submit) so two listeners never race on one click.
notes: WooCommerce/EDD/FluentCart rails are PRO-only. Free ships standalone + Stripe + PayPal + Offline + Test.

promise: A buyer paying offline sees the owner's instructions immediately, can upload proof, and the order is not left in limbo.

entry_points.frontend: order view offline instructions + proof upload
entry_points.admin: Sell Services > Orders > Mark as Paid

ux_bar: payment_method is written the moment offline is chosen and is NEVER NULL - a NULL here is a dead end no admin screen and no buyer view can resolve. Marking paid twice credits the vendor exactly once (row-locked claim).
notes: The NULL payment_method case was a real fatal-class defect.

promise: A declined card shows the buyer the real reason and lets them immediately try another method, with no order silently created for an unpaid charge.
ux_bar: The message is Stripe's own decline reason (filterable via wpss_payment_declined_message), never a generic 'Payment failed'. A requires_payment_method with no prior attempt is an UNFINISHED flow, not a decline - the two are distinguished by last_payment_error so a buyer is never blamed for a card problem that did not happen.

promise: A buyer returning from 3D-Secure sees the true outcome of their payment rather than a blank form they could pay through twice.
ux_bar: Exactly ONE of three states renders: paid (link to order, no form), processing (auto-refresh, explicit 'do not pay again', no Pay button), or genuinely unpaid (the only state offering 'try another method'). The webhook is the source of truth; this page never re-decides what already happened.

promise: A buyer can pay for one specific existing order (accepted proposal, milestone phase, extension or tip) through a dedicated pay link.
ux_bar: Only the owning buyer reaches the pay screen; an already-paid order shows 'already paid' rather than a live Pay button that would double-charge; a LOCKED milestone phase is refused SERVER-side even when the buyer hand-crafts the URL - the lock is never just a hidden button.

promise: Checkout is fully usable on a phone and never scrolls sideways.
ux_bar: At <=1024px the 'what happens next' steps and the order summary render BEFORE the payment form in source order, so a buyer sees what they are paying and what follows before choosing how to pay. At <=768px the trust-badge bar wraps rather than widening the page. documentElement.scrollWidth === clientWidth at 390px.
notes: Two prior regressions on this exact surface: Basecamp 10208392848 (guarantees-bar overflow) and 10304335437 (payment before summary, fixed in 1.7.2 e4feba50).

promise: A theme that opens its own content container never makes checkout render full-bleed or double-padded.
ux_bar: On a theme that opens its container in a page template (stock Twenty Twenty-Four), the plugin's wrapper constrains and centres. On a theme with its own container (BuddyX), the wrapper stands down (max-width:none) rather than nesting a second gutter.
notes: Previously passed on BuddyX 'by luck, not design' - MUST be re-verified on a plain theme, not only the house theme.

promise: With no gateway enabled, a buyer reaching checkout is told clearly rather than shown an empty payment form.
ux_bar: The notice explicitly says to contact support rather than rendering an empty method list with no explanation.

promise: A buyer can send the vendor a tip after an order, using preset amounts or a custom one.

entry_points.frontend: order view Send a Tip modal

ux_bar: Clicking a preset FILLS the amount field visibly rather than submitting immediately, so the buyer can still edit before sending. Two rapid clicks credit the vendor once (idempotency key).

promise: A buyer sees all their orders in one dashboard list, filterable by status.
ux_bar: Paginated server-side, not an unbounded fetch. An empty list explains that placing an order populates it and links to browse services. The ACTIVE filter chip stays readable on themes that recolour content links (>= 4.5:1).
notes: Contrast measured 3.00 under BuddyX before the 1.7.2 fix (6017b9e1); RTL sibling sheet was stale until this release.

promise: A vendor sees all their sales in one dashboard list, filterable by status.
ux_bar: A dual-role member lands on the section matching how they clicked in - My Orders never silently lands them on Sales or vice versa.
notes: 1.7.0 regression: wpss_append_dashboard_section dropped the 'orders' default.

promise: After paying, a buyer is taken to a requirements form, and the order does not move to in-progress until it is submitted.

entry_points.frontend: post-checkout redirect; later via order view Submit Requirements

ux_bar: A progress indicator shows N of M required answered and fills as they type. The route stays reachable LATER from the order view even for a service with no custom fields - never a dead end reachable only via the one-time post-payment redirect. A Yes/No requirement offers BOTH answers, and a required Yes/No can be answered No.
notes: 1.7.2 (26082a6e): Yes/No previously rendered only Yes, so a required Yes/No had exactly one possible answer.

promise: A buyer can skip submitting requirements and let the vendor start without them.
ux_bar: DEAD ON WEB. No Skip control exists in requirements-form.php or order-view.php, so every web buyer must submit something even on a service where required_count is 0. Either wire the control or remove the promise.
notes: Verified 2026-09-19: route at src/API/OrdersController.php:247; zero references to 'requirements/skip' in templates/ or assets/js/.

promise: A buyer attaching a reference file to a requirement can change their mind, and the file they end up seeing is the file that gets submitted.
ux_bar: Choosing a second file REPLACES the first, visibly, and input.files holds the new one - the form must never submit a file the buyer already replaced. Dropping more files than the field accepts keeps the allowed number and STATES how many were refused rather than discarding them silently.
notes: 1.7.2 (77945389): handleFiles() appended and stopped at the cap, so on a 1-file field the second pick was discarded and the ORIGINAL file was submitted. Silent data loss, reported only as unclear feedback.

promise: A vendor can start work on a paid order whose requirements are in.
ux_bar: Start Working shows exactly when status is accepted or requirements_submitted - never vetoed by a second unrelated status whitelist. A documented former bug made this button unreachable after the buyer submitted requirements.

promise: A vendor can deliver finished work with a message and file attachments, moving the order to buyer review.
ux_bar: Files are genuinely attached (multipart processed via wpss_normalize_uploaded_files) - a delivery is never accepted as delivered with a file COUNT but no actual attachment. The buyer sees the state change without a manual refresh.
notes: 1.2.0 KG-7 fixed exactly this: the prior integer-ID files arg never attached anything.

promise: A buyer can accept a delivery and complete the order.
ux_bar: Offered only on pending_approval; once accepted the button set CHANGES to the terminal state (Write a Review appears) rather than the same actions persisting on a finished order.

promise: A buyer can request a revision instead of accepting, and can see how many remain.

entry_points.frontend: order view Request Revision (labelled with remaining count)

ux_bar: The badge changes state at the LAST revision and again when exhausted ('All N revisions used') - a buyer never discovers they are out only after clicking. While a revision is pending the action area shows a disabled 'Waiting for Revised Delivery', not a repeatable button that could double-request.

promise: A buyer can cancel an order outright before meaningful work has started.
ux_bar: Cancel confirms first via the shared wpssConfirm dialog, not a bare browser confirm() - it is destructive and, on a paid order, triggers a refund.

promise: A buyer can request cancellation of an in-progress order within 24 hours if nothing has been delivered.
ux_bar: The button DISAPPEARS (not merely disables) once the window closes or a delivery exists, so a buyer is never invited to click something guaranteed to fail server-side.

promise: A vendor can accept or dispute a buyer's cancellation request, and the buyer sees a clear pending state meanwhile.

entry_points.frontend: order view Accept/Dispute Cancellation (vendor); buyer sees a disabled Cancellation Pending notice

ux_bar: The buyer's pending state is a disabled control WITH explanatory text ('Waiting for vendor response'), never a missing action that reads as the request having vanished.

promise: Buyer and vendor can message on an order thread with text and image attachments, updating live.
ux_bar: A sent message appears without a manual reload and the thread polls for replies. The unread badge genuinely reflects unread count - a documented past bug hid a correct badge behind text-indent:-999999px.

promise: A buyer or vendor can open a dispute on an order that has gone wrong.
ux_bar: Open Dispute and View Dispute are mutually exclusive by the order's ACTUAL dispute state - a past bug hid View Dispute on disputed orders because an unrelated outer status whitelist vetoed it.

promise: Either party can respond and attach evidence to an open dispute.
ux_bar: Choosing a file shows its filename beside the attach button BEFORE submitting, so a party can confirm the right file rather than submitting blind.

promise: The party who opened a dispute can withdraw it, and either party can escalate it for admin attention with a reason.

roles.vendor: can escalate; cannot withdraw unless opener

ux_bar: Each control is ABSENT for anyone the API would refuse - Withdraw shows only to the opener, and only while open/pending/escalated. Escalate collects the reason in the plugin's own modal BEFORE sending, so the buyer never gets a late server rejection for something the form should have caught. Both confirm first.
notes: 1.7.2 (47c90b98): both capabilities existed in the API since launch with NO UI at all. The original fix used window.prompt() for the reason (unstyleable, inaccessible, blocks automation) and built the URL from a nonexistent wpssData.restUrl, producing a 404 - both corrected before release. This row is the reason the catalog exists.

promise: The site owner can review, assign and resolve any dispute.
ux_bar: The outcome is recorded on the order TIMELINE visible to both parties, not only inside the admin screen - neither party should have to contact support to learn what was decided.
notes: A real fatal shipped in 1.7.0: Dispute::get_resolution_label() called a method that exists only on DisputeService, faulting on any resolved dispute. Re-verify resolution-label rendering end to end.

promise: A buyer can leave a rating and review after an order completes.
ux_bar: Reachable only from a genuinely completed order, never mid-progress. With moderation on, the buyer is TOLD their review is pending rather than it silently vanishing from the public list.

promise: On a request order, a vendor can propose a phased contract, and each phase is submitted, approved and paid in lock-step.

entry_points.frontend: order view Propose/Submit Milestone + per-phase Pay

ux_bar: A locked phase shows NO live Pay button, and a hand-crafted pay URL for it is refused server-side with an explanation ('pay the previous phase first'). Approving the final phase auto-completes the parent order with no separate manual step. Cancelling every phase must NOT complete the order.
notes: 1.7.2 (57eb9009): auto-complete now requires a phase to have actually been DELIVERED - cancelling every phase previously completed the order and blocked proposing a new one. Mutually exclusive with paid extensions on the same order.

promise: On a catalog order, a vendor can quote extra paid work with extra days, and the buyer can accept or decline.

entry_points.frontend: order view Request Extension / Accept-Decline card

ux_bar: Accepting visibly pushes the delivery deadline out by the quoted days ON THE SAME SCREEN - a buyer never has to cross-reference the original deadline against the extension to know when to expect delivery.
notes: templates/order/order-view.php still contains 4 raw alert() calls (around lines 1959 and 1984) where the rest of the page uses the shared toast/confirm system. Inconsistent with the plugin's own admin-ux rule.

promise: The site owner can create an order manually on a buyer's behalf.

entry_points.admin: Sell Services > Orders > Create Manual Order

ux_bar: A manual order enters the SAME lifecycle and status machine as a checkout order - it is not a parallel order type the rest of the UI fails to recognise. Its commission rate is pinned at creation so a later global change never rewrites history.

promise: Both parties can see a chronological timeline of everything that happened on an order.
ux_bar: Every entry shows a human-readable date, never blank or a raw MySQL timestamp.
notes: The web view builds its own PHP timeline rather than calling the REST route that exists for app clients - TWO implementations of one list. Confirm they never disagree when either changes.

promise: A sub-order (tip, extension, milestone phase) shows a simplified flow, not the full catalog-order lifecycle.
ux_bar: The stepper shows exactly 2 steps (pay, done) rather than the standard 5 - requirements and delivery never apply to a one-shot credit.
